chunks: A man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have acquired wealth in which I was not scrupulous. Is there repentance for me?”
He said: “Bring me its khums.” So he brought him its khums.
Then he said: “It is yours. Indeed, when a man repents, his wealth repents with him.”

key_terms.أَغْمَضْتُ: I acted without full scrupulousness or caution regarding its source
key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.مَالًا: wealth or property that the man had acquired

ai.seo_question: Can a person repent after acquiring wealth through questionable means, and what role does khums play?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that a man asked Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام about repentance after acquiring wealth through dubious means. He was instructed to give its khums, after which the Imam عليه السلام affirmed that sincere repentance restores the person's standing, and his wealth is accepted with him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1655 - A man came to Amir al-Mu'minin (Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as)) and said:
"O Amir al-Mu'minin, I have acquired wealth through questionable means. Is there repentance for me?"

The Imam (as) replied: "Bring me its Khums."
The man brought him the Khums,
and the Imam (as) said: "It is yours. When a person repents, his wealth repents with him."
